data.content_ref: inline:The analogy's overturn conditions include proving the decentralized network's shared-cause failure rate is lower than the monolith's internal coordination failure rate. But a lower failure rate is not the same as lower resilience to correlated failure: the problem asks which architecture is more resilient to correlated failure and how to distinguish truly independent from merely-appearing-uncorrelated failures. The target offers rate-comparison thresholds without identifying what evidence distinguishes genuine independence from hidden shared causes, so the evidentiary clause is unmet even when the analogy stands.
